title: Journal v2: schema-validated, indexed, replayable event log
summary: The journal is rebuilt around a versioned event envelope: ten payload types (run-started, verification, review, review-answer, review-decision, finding, state-change, run-complete, attention, checkpoint-complete), an actor that is a harness, a person or the engine itself, and optional work item, change and cost. Every appended event is validated against a JSON Schema before a byte is written, the first accepted event records the run in a per-work-item index under a file lock, and a run-complete event must name the journal's current head hash and closes the run. The chain hash now covers the whole payload (durations, cache, cost, transcripts included) and a second digest, the replay digest, covers only the decision fields, so two runs of the same decisions share a digest while their chain heads differ. The buffer directory becomes runs/, and a reader replays a run, checking every link before returning any event.

lanes.label: Callers
lanes.subtitle: engine commands that write events
lanes.summary: The checkpoint runner and the review runner are the two writers; both now build an Actor and go through the same validated append path.

lanes.label: Journal
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/journal
lanes.summary: The journal module split into event model, hash, schema validation, index and reader, with the writer in journal.rs.

lanes.label: State directory
lanes.subtitle: ~/.osf/state
lanes.summary: The on-disk layout: runs/<run>.jsonl for journals, index/<sha256>.json for per-work-item run lists, each with a lock file.

lanes.label: CI
lanes.subtitle: GitHub Actions
lanes.summary: The checkpoint-evidence artifact now uploads the runs directory instead of the old buffer directory.

nodes.label: Checkpoint runner
nodes.subtitle: osf verify --checkpoint
nodes.summary: Runs the checkpoint's moon tasks and writes one verification event per task plus one checkpoint-complete event. Now builds Actor::system("osf") and fills the new check_type, summary and EvidenceGrade fields.

nodes.label: Review runner
nodes.subtitle: osf review
nodes.summary: Writes one review-answer event per judged attempt and one review-decision event for the whole review, now through Actor::system.

nodes.label: Journal writer
nodes.subtitle: Journal::append / append_draft
nodes.summary: Computes the chain hash, validates the serialised event against the schema, refuses a run-complete whose head_hash is not the current head, records the run in the index on the first accepted event, and refuses any event after run-complete. A refused event writes no byte and leaves the head unchanged.

nodes.label: Event model
nodes.subtitle: Event, Actor, Cost, Payload
nodes.summary: The versioned envelope and its ten payload types, the three actor kinds, the four evidence grades, the work item states and blocked causes, and the EventDraft a caller supplies.

nodes.label: Hash chain
nodes.subtitle: event_hash, ReplayDigest
nodes.summary: SHA-256 over prev_hash, a newline and the canonical JSON of payload, work item, change, actor and cost. The replay digest is a second SHA-256 over each event's decision line, with timings, cache, cost, run ids and transcripts removed.

nodes.label: Schema validator
nodes.subtitle: journal::schema::validate
nodes.summary: Compiles event.schema.json once per process and checks every event before it is written, returning one reason per problem. The schema encodes the cross-field rules: a harness actor needs a model, a blocked state change needs a cause, only observed findings may name a verifier.

nodes.label: Run index
nodes.subtitle: record_run, runs_for_work_item
nodes.summary: One JSON file per work item, named by the SHA-256 of the work item id, listing its run ids in recorded order. Writes go through a temporary file renamed over the target, under an fs4 file lock held for up to ten seconds.

nodes.label: Journal reader
nodes.subtitle: read_run
nodes.summary: Replays a run's journal, checking each line's schema, run id, prev_hash and recomputed hash before returning any event, and refusing a line after run-complete. Returns the events, the head hash, the replay digest and whether the run completed.

nodes.label: runs/
nodes.subtitle: <state_dir>/runs/<run>.jsonl
nodes.summary: The journal file per run, one JSON event per line. Renamed from buffer/; a run id must be a safe single path component, so no separators, no .., no leading or trailing dot and no Windows device name.

nodes.label: index/
nodes.subtitle: <state_dir>/index/<sha256>.json
nodes.summary: Per-work-item run lists, each with a sibling .lock file. Created only when a journal carries a work item.

nodes.label: checkpoint-evidence artifact
nodes.subtitle: upload-artifact
nodes.summary: Uploads $OSF_STATE_DIR/runs and .osf/out, so the evidence artifact follows the renamed directory.

edges.label: append(actor, payload)
edges.summary: Each task result and the checkpoint-complete event go through the validated append path.

edges.label: append(actor, payload)
edges.summary: Review answers and the review decision go through the same path.

edges.label: validate(event)
edges.summary: Every event is serialised to JSON and checked against the schema before the line is written; a failure returns the reasons and writes nothing.

edges.label: event_hash(HashInput)
edges.summary: The chain hash is computed from the previous hash and the canonical JSON of the event's hashed parts.

edges.label: record_run(work_item, run)
edges.summary: The first accepted event records the run in its work item's index before the journal line lands, so a failed index update refuses the event.

edges.label: one JSON line
edges.summary: The validated event is appended as one line to runs/<run>.jsonl.

edges.label: rename over target
edges.summary: The index is written through a temporary file renamed over the target, under a lock file.

edges.label: read_to_string
edges.summary: The reader loads the run's journal file and checks every line in order.

edges.label: validate(line)
edges.summary: Each line is checked against the same schema the writer used before it is accepted.

edges.label: event_hash + ReplayDigest
edges.summary: The reader recomputes each event's chain hash and accumulates the replay digest over the decision lines.

edges.label: shares validate_run_id
edges.summary: The reader and the index share the run id check, so a run id that cannot be indexed cannot be read either.

edges.label: $OSF_STATE_DIR/runs
edges.summary: The CI artifact path follows the renamed directory.

flows.title: Appending one validated event
flows.summary: What happens between a caller handing over a payload and a line landing in the run's journal, including the two refusals that leave the file untouched.

messages.label: event_hash(prev_hash, payload, work_item, change, actor, cost)
messages.note: The chain hash covers the whole payload, so a changed duration or cache outcome changes the hash.

messages.label: validate(event JSON)
messages.note: A schema failure returns the reasons and writes no byte; the chain head is unchanged.

messages.label: run-complete head_hash == current head?
messages.note: A run-complete event naming any other hash is refused, and once one is accepted no later event is accepted.

messages.label: record_run(work_item, run)
messages.note: Only on the first accepted event, and only when the journal carries a work item. A failed index update refuses the event before any line is written.

flows.title: Replaying a run
flows.summary: How a reader turns a journal file back into events, and why two runs of the same decisions share a replay digest but not a chain head.

messages.label: recompute event_hash, compare prev_hash
messages.note: A tampered payload, a changed duration, a deleted or swapped line all break the chain at their own line number.

messages.label: ReplayDigest over decision lines
messages.note: Timings, cache, cost, run ids and transcripts are dropped, so two runs of the same decisions share a digest while their chain heads differ.

messages.label: events, head_hash, replay_digest, complete
messages.note: Any failure returns that line's error and no events at all, so a caller never sees a partial chain.

steps.heading: Two writers, one path
steps.body: Checkpoint and review both build an Actor and append through the same validated writer.

steps.heading: Nothing invalid is written
steps.body: The event is serialised and checked against the schema before any byte lands.

steps.heading: The run is indexed first
steps.body: The first accepted event records the run in its work item's index, or the event is refused.

steps.heading: One line, one chain link
steps.body: The validated event is appended to runs/<run>.jsonl with its prev_hash and hash.

steps.heading: Replay checks every link
steps.body: The reader validates and re-hashes each line before returning any event.

steps.heading: Decisions, not timings
steps.body: The replay digest drops timings, cache, cost and run ids, so identical decisions match.
